entities.summary:
Cyprus is a sovereign nation in West Asia, Asia. Its capital is Nicosia (Lefkosia/Lefkoşa) — last divided capital in Europe. Official languages include Greek, Turkish. Government: Unitary presidential constitutional republic (de facto divided: Republic of Cyprus controls south; Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus in north, recognised only by Türkiye).

Population: approximately 1.3 million. Area: 9,251 km². Comprehensive index for Cyprus covering Bronze Age Alashiya (copper trade), Mycenaean-Achaean colonisation, Phoenician Kition, Assyrian/Egyptian/Persian rule, Hellenistic Ptolemaic period, Roman province (Paphos), Byzantine era, Richard the Lionheart/Lusignan Crusader kingdom, Venetian rule, Ottoman conquest 1571, British colony 1878, EOKA/Enosis, independence 1960, intercommunal violence, Turkish invasion 1974, division (Green Line), EU accession 2004 (acquis suspended for north), and reunification talks.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Cyprus played a significant role in the copper trade during the Bronze Age and was later colonized by various powers including the Romans and Ottomans. Its modern-day division has had lasting implications for regional politics.
